summary: Lynn Teskey Denton worked in Indology and religious studies. She earned a B.A. from McMaster University and a B.Litt. from Somerville College (1973–1975). She taught at McMaster University and served as Assistant Professor at Concordia University (1984–1989).

Lynn Thomas is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She earned a BA and MA from Lancaster University and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford in 1987. She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton.

László Gaál was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He earned a Ph.D. at Franz Joseph University and studied at Göttingen under Friedrich Carl Andreas, Emil Sieg, and Richard Fick. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University and Debrecen.

Léon Feer specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying under Philippe Édouard Foucaux, Théodore Pavie, Julius Mohl, and Étienne Marc Quatremère. He held posts at the INALCO, Collège de France, EPHE, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
Léon Rodet was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the École Polytechnique around 1851–1853 and was a member of the Société Asiatique.

Léon Vandermeersch was a sinologist and philosopher who studied at INALCO, the University of Paris, and EPHE. He held posts at the National Museum of Vietnamese History, Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, EPHE, the Maison Franco-Japonaise, and directed the EFEO (1989–1993).

Léonard Eugène Aurousseau was a sinologist and historian who studied at EPHE and INALCO under Édouard Chavannes. He spent his career at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, serving as a teacher and later as Director from 1926 to 1929.

Lê Mạnh Thát is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history. He earned a BA at the University of Saigon and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison before holding a post at Vạn Hạnh University from around 1974 to 1975.

M. A. Mehendale was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India and held multiple posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, including Professor of Sanskrit and Professor of Sanskrit (Vedic) Literature.
M. Athar Ali was a historian and Indologist. He completed his studies at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1947 to 1953 and subsequently worked there as a historian from around 1953 to 1990.

M. D. Balasubrahmanyam, a scholar in Indology and linguistics, earned a dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University. He held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, as Reader at Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha, and as Principal at Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan.

M. H. Krishna was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, the University of Madras, and University College London under Ernest Arthur Gardner. He served as Professor of History and Dean of Arts at the University of Mysore.

M. M. McCabe is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She served as a Fellow at Murray Edwards College, Professor at King's College London (1990–2014), and Keeling Scholar and Honorary Professor at University College London.

M. R. Raghava Varier is a scholar of history, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the Archaeological Survey of India, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Calicut, where he later served as Professor from around 1976 to 1996.

M. S. A. Rao worked in Indology and related fields. He studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held posts at the University of Delhi (around 1955–1985), Pennsylvania, and Syracuse.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Mysore and Savitribai Phule Pune University under M. N. Deshpande. He worked at Karnatak University, the Karnataka State Archaeology Department, and served as Director General of the ASI.

M. Seshagiri Sastri was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University.
M. Shinoda is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied under Seiren Matsunami and also studied at Agoura High School and the Art Center College of Design.

M. Victor Stanley was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Lawrence University, Wisconsin-Madison, Oregon, and Yale University. He served as Supervising-Principal at Corona-Norco Unified School District.

M. Yamunacharya was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under Mysore Hiriyanna, Ardeshir Ruttonji Wadia, and Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He served as Professor in Philosophy at Maharaja's College, Mysore.
